summary.headline: Sapphire Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% to INR 888 crore and adjusted EBITDA 37% to INR 75 crore, with SSSG positive across KFC (5%), Pizza Hut (1%) and Sri Lanka (9%).
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was the second consecutive quarter of strong performance, with consolidated revenue up 15% to INR 888 crore and adjusted EBITDA up 37% to INR 75 crore (8.4% margin). Positive SSSG across all three brand verticals drove the improvement, helped by lower discounts since October 2025 and 2-3% price increases taken in April-June. Sri Lanka profitability weakened on rupee depreciation, minimum wage increases and higher energy costs linked to the Middle East crisis. Management said demand has been broadly stable rather than improving, with June weaker than April and May.

financial_highlights.change: gross margin up 220 bps; restaurant EBITDA down YoY

segments.name: KFC India
segments.commentary: SSSG 5%, revenue up 17%, gross margin up 160 bps QoQ; 16 KFC restaurants added; dine-in and takeaway mix rose from 57% to 59%. Digital kiosks in about 75% of stores.

segments.name: Pizza Hut India
segments.commentary: SSSG 1%, the first positive print after five quarters of positive SSSG; revenue up 3%, gross margin up 80 bps; 5 restaurants added. Dine-in and takeaway mix flat at 50%. Restaurant EBITDA was -3.6%.

segments.name: Sri Lanka
segments.commentary: SSSG 9%, revenue up 14% in LKR terms, gross margin up 220 bps, but restaurant EBITDA of 12% fell on energy and wage inflation and rupee depreciation. One restaurant added. Management guides high single-digit growth for the year.

guidance_outlook: KFC store expansion guidance of 60-80 stores per year unchanged.
Pizza Hut expansion stays cautious; calendar 2026 store additions expected to be near zero, pending a unified strategy between the two franchisees and CCI approval.
Sri Lanka profitability normalisation expected at least a couple of quarters away; management said the store plan is unchanged for the year.
Management is focused on driving SSSG rather than pushing restaurant margin back to 17-19%; KFC is expected to grow 15-20% if SSSG holds at 5-6%.
Management said the Pizza Hut global sale by Yum! does not affect existing franchise agreements.
capex_capacity: KFC added 16 restaurants and Pizza Hut added 5 in India and 1 in Sri Lanka in Q1; total restaurants at 1,074 as of 30 June 2026.
KFC targets 60-80 store additions per year. Management aims to double the KFC store count over five years.
KFC new stores in smaller towns have about 20% lower ADS than Tier 1 metros, but lower operating costs give similar payback and profitability, per management.
Store-opening decisions are guided by new-store strike rates: ADS and payback at one year, with 75-80% of a cohort meeting targets.
Pizza Hut expansion was 50-60 stores in an earlier period, fell to 20-30, and was near zero in calendar 2025.
demand_pricing: Management said demand has not materially improved and has stayed similar; April and May were good, June was weaker, and July was good, helped by an earlier Shravan start.
Price increases were about 2% for KFC and 2-3% for Pizza Hut, taken in instalments (KFC 1% in April, 0.5-1% in June). Management said there has been no major impact on SSSG so far.
Combined price increase and lower discounts add about 50 bps to 1% to the customer bill; APC was stable.
Same-store transaction growth exceeded SSSG, and dine-in and takeaway are growing faster than delivery. Management does not disclose the split of SSSG between transactions and ticket size.
No heightened discounting seen on the two aggregators in recent quarters. Management says delivery pricing has moved closer to dine-in pricing.

qa_highlights.question: How should the demand environment be read, given KFC SSSG of 5% against 6% last quarter, and how is the quarter trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is similar to before with no material improvement. April and May were good, June was weaker, and July is good. Upside is attributed to internal sales initiatives.

qa_highlights.question: What will it take to normalise Sri Lanka profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will prioritise transaction growth and absorb short-term cost-of-sales pressure. Normalisation is expected at least a couple of quarters away, with recovery through pricing or lower input costs.

qa_highlights.question: At what SSSG does operating leverage start, and what restaurant margin level is needed to return to 18-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Leverage typically starts at 3-5% SSSG, with efficiencies helping at that range. ADS growth tracks SSSG, and management's near-term focus is SSSG, not a margin target of 18%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the Yum! global Pizza Hut sale affect the master franchise agreement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the parent-level sale does not affect current franchise agreements and sees the new owner as a potential positive for brand investment.

qa_highlights.question: Is the SSSG recovery broad-based across geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the recovery has been broad-based over the last two quarters, driven partly by consumer sentiment and partly by value campaigns. Pizza Hut's four-course meal and BOGO offers drove dine-in and takeaway.

qa_highlights.question: What are the KFC expansion plans and the smaller-city unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: KFC guidance of 60-80 stores per year is unchanged. Smaller-town stores have about 20% lower ADS, but similar payback and profitability because costs are also lower.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Pizza Hut turnaround plan and has Tamil Nadu performance differed?
qa_highlights.answer: No new Pizza Hut steps. Tamil Nadu, an exclusive territory with extra marketing, has delivered double-digit SSSG and restaurant EBITDA outperformance, and that continues in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Given the raw material situation, are further price increases needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is happy with the current price increases. It passes on only 50-60% of inflation, managing the rest through efficiencies, and may absorb the impact in restaurant EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is KFC's growth divergence from aggregator growth likely to persist?
qa_highlights.answer: KFC is back at 17% growth as SSSG recovers. With 5-6% SSSG, management sees KFC matching 15-20% growth, while Pizza Hut needs a unified strategy before it can expand.

qa_highlights.question: Is Sri Lanka's FY27 high single-digit growth guidance changing given inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Sri Lanka guidance remains high single-digit. A single weak profitability quarter will not change the store-opening plan for the year.

risks_watch: Sustainability of KFC SSSG at 5-6% after a 6% prior quarter; management said demand is similar, June was weaker than April and May, and July's strength was partly a Shravan timing effect.
Sri Lanka restaurant EBITDA at 12% under rupee depreciation, minimum wage hikes and Middle East-linked energy costs; management guides at least a couple of quarters before normalisation.
Pizza Hut expansion stays near zero for calendar 2026, pending a unified strategy between the two franchisees and CCI approval; the Yum! global sale outcome is a watch item.

Pricing headroom: price increases of about 2-3% pass only 50-60% of inflation, and management said further increases depend on how the conflict-driven raw material situation evolves over the next two quarters.

Restaurant margin recovery to 17-19% is not the near-term target; monitor whether new-store strike rates (ADS and one-year payback, 75-80% of cohort meeting targets) hold as smaller-town stores run about 20% lower ADS.
key_quotes: Q1 FY '27 was our second consecutive quarter of strong performance with 15% revenue growth, best in the last eleven quarters and 32% adjusted EBITDA growth, best in the last fifteen quarters.
So I don't think there's been any material improvement in the demand environment. I would say it has remained similar.
Currently, the focus is not to get back immediate ly to 17%, 18% or 19% margin. I think the entire focus over the last few quarters has been to get the SSSG back.

So we would typically restrict our price hikes to 50% to 60% of the inflation, and the rest of the impact we would try and manage through efficiencies on our supply chain and efficiencies through other lines on the P&L.
summary.management_tone: Confident on KFC and the SSSG recovery, citing the two-pronged value strategy and dine-in/takeaway growth. Cautious on demand (no material improvement, June weaker) and on Sri Lanka profitability, where management described the hit as short term. Evasive on the SSSG split between transactions and ticket size and on specific ADS thresholds for margin recovery.

adds.what: KFC restaurant additions: 60-80 stores per year (16 added in Q1 FY27)
Pizza Hut India restaurant additions (5 added in Q1); further expansion near zero for calendar 2026 pending CCI approval and unified franchisee strategy
Sri Lanka restaurant addition (1 in Q1); store plan unchanged for the year, no count given

growth.why: KFC guided 15-20% growth if SSSG holds at 5-6%, backed by the reaffirmed 60-80 store per year plan (16 added in Q1) and 2-3% pricing, though management said demand was flat and June was weaker, and Pizza Hut expansion is near zero for CY26.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Restaurant EBITDA margin rose to 13% (up 80 bps) and KFC gross margin rose 160 bps QoQ, but management is focused on SSSG rather than the 17-19% margin target, operating leverage only starts at 3-5% SSSG, and Sri Lanka margin is at 12%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: KFC added 16 restaurants in Q1 and 60-80 store additions per year is guided and unchanged, with total restaurants at 1,074 as of 30 June 2026; Pizza Hut calendar 2026 additions are near zero pending CCI approval.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: KFC SSSG at 5% with same-store transactions growing faster than SSSG, 16 KFC and 5 Pizza Hut restaurants added in Q1, and 60-80 KFC stores per year guided; Pizza Hut volume growth is limited by near-zero expansion in CY26.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex utilisation was not disclosed and no new capex plan was announced; KFC's 60-80 store plan is already committed, so new capex would only be announced if Pizza Hut's unified strategy or CCI approval clears.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: KFC is guided to grow 15-20% if SSSG holds at 5-6% (Q1 revenue up 17%), but management said demand has not materially improved, so an upgrade depends on SSSG beating 6%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: June was weaker than April and May with demand flat, KFC SSSG fell to 5% from 6%, and Sri Lanka restaurant EBITDA fell to 12% on rupee depreciation, wage hikes and energy costs, with normalisation at least a couple of quarters away.

rows.label: Price increases of 2-3% with lower discounts passing 50-60% of inflation
rows.why: Price increases of about 2% for KFC and 2-3% for Pizza Hut, with combined price and discount changes adding 50 bps to 1% to the bill and no major SSSG impact so far; further increases depend on raw material trends over the next two quarters.

rows.label: Pizza Hut CCI approval and Yum! global sale
rows.why: Pizza Hut expansion stays near zero for calendar 2026 pending CCI approval and a unified franchisee strategy, while management says the Yum! global sale does not affect existing franchise agreements.

rows.label: KFC smaller-town expansion
rows.why: Smaller-town KFC stores run about 20% lower ADS than Tier 1 metros but show similar payback and profitability, supporting continued store additions within the 60-80 per year plan.

tone.note: Management was confident on KFC SSSG recovery (5%, 17% revenue growth) and the two-pronged value strategy, but cautious on demand (flat, June weaker) and Sri Lanka profitability (12% restaurant EBITDA); analysts pushed on SSSG sustainability, pricing headroom, margin targets and Pizza Hut expansion.
